title: D.C. circuits
main_stem: A battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) $9.6\mathrm{V}$ and negligible internal resistance is connected in series with two fixed resistors and a thermistor, as shown in Fig. 7.1. [Fig. 7.1 shows a series loop: $9.6\mathrm{V}$ battery at top, $5800\,\Omega$ resistor on right, thermistor at bottom right, $3400\,\Omega$ resistor at bottom left, with a voltmeter $V$ connected across the $3400\,\Omega$ resistor and thermistor combination.] The fixed resistors have resistances of $3400\,\Omega$ and $5800\,\Omega$. The reading on the voltmeter in the circuit is $6.0\mathrm{V}$.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Calculate the current in the resistor of resistance $5800\,\Omega$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Calculate the resistance of the thermistor.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem: The initial energy stored in the battery is $2.6 \times 10^{4}\,\mathrm{J}$. Assume that the e.m.f. of the battery is constant.
parts.text: Determine the final energy stored in the battery after a charge of $330\,\mathrm{C}$ has moved through it.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.part_stem: The environmental conditions change causing an increase in the resistance of the thermistor. State whether there is a decrease, increase or no change to:

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.part_stem: The environmental conditions change causing an increase in the resistance of the thermistor. State whether there is a decrease, increase or no change to:

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.part_stem: The environmental conditions change causing an increase in the resistance of the thermistor. State whether there is a decrease, increase or no change to:
parts.text: the potential difference across the thermistor.
